neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with others, abducted the victim, tied him with chains, and threatened to kill him if ransom was not paid. The victim was kept in captivity for almost two days, during which he was interrogated by the abductors and threatened with death. The victim was eventually released after the ransom was paid. The police recovered various items, including currency notes, firearms, and a car, from the accused. The victim identified the accused during trial, despite initially not naming them. The prosecution presented evidence of the victim's testimony, the recovery of items, and the involvement of the accused in the conspiracy to extract ransom under threat of harm.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the evidence of the victim was truthful and detailed, establishing the complicity of the accused in the abduction and ransom plot. The victim's testimony, along with the recovery of items like currency notes, firearms, and the Honda City car from the accused, supported the prosecution's case. The call details, though challenged, were not essential to proving the charges against the accused.

quotes.text: The evidence of the victim as a whole, is truthful, having regard to the details provided with accompanying clarity and conviction. His elaborate testimony has remained unshaken substantially even by his cross-examination.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the victim's failure to name the appellant at the initial stage and the omission of the investigating agency to hold the TIP (Taluka Police Inspector) were fatal to the prosecution case. They also claimed that the victim's identification of the appellant at trial was insufficient and that the call details were inadmissible, undermining the prosecution's evidence.

quotes.text: The omission on the part of the victim to mention at the first instance the name of appellant, having regard to the charge of conspiracy and the concerted steps, to actualise the same is of no fatal bearing on the prosecution case.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that conspiracy requires an act (actus reus) and a mental state (mens rea). It emphasized that conspirators do not need to know all details of the plot, but must be co-participants in the main object, with unity of purpose and participation at different stages.

quotes.text: Conspiracy requires an act i.e. actus reus and an accompanying mental state i.e. mens rea. Whereas the agreement constitutes the act, the intention to achieve the unlawful objectives of the agreement comprises the required mental state.

The courts below correctly analyzed the evidence, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with the conviction and sentence.
